key_insight: Graph Sparse Sampling reuses shared sampled futures across candidate actions to avoid the exponential horizon blow-up of tree-based planning in continuous MDPs.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more scalable online control strategy for autonomous systems, with GPU-friendly batching and polynomial horizon dependence under suitable conditions.
method: Build a branch-free graph instead of a search tree, sharing successor samples across actions.
Use smoothed backups with finite-sample guarantees for full-rank or low-rank simulators.
Support discrete or sampled continuous actions while focusing computation with heuristics and overlap assumptions.
evidence_signal: In continuous-control simulations, GSS substantially outperformed tree-based planners on long horizons or achieved near-optimal performance.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on overlap, regularity, and action-coverage conditions, so performance may degrade when those assumptions are not met.
paper_title: Graph Sparse Sampling: Breaking the Curse of the Horizon in Continuous MDP Planning
